func TestProbeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	for _, c := range roundTripCases() {
		func() {
			defer func() {
				if r := recover(); r != nil {
					t.Logf("%-42s => PANIC %v", c.name, r)
				}
			}()
			if _, err := actions_module.GetEventsFromContent([]byte(c.content)); err != nil {
				t.Logf("%-42s => REJECTED at detection (workflow never triggers): %v", c.name, err)
				return
			}
			wfs, err := jobparser.Parse([]byte(c.content))
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("%-42s => parse err: %v", c.name, err)
				return
			}
			if len(wfs) == 0 {
				t.Logf("%-42s => 0 jobs (status of a run with no jobs: %q)", c.name, actions_model.AggregateJobStatus(nil).String())
				return
			}
			problems := []string{}
			for _, wf := range wfs {
				id, job := wf.Job()
				origRuns := []string{}
				for _, s := range job.Steps {
					origRuns = append(origRuns, s.Run)
				}
				if err := wf.SetJob(id, job.EraseNeeds()); err != nil {
					problems = append(problems, fmt.Sprintf("%s: SetJob: %v", job.Name, err))
					continue
				}
				payload, err := wf.Marshal()
				if err != nil {
					problems = append(problems, fmt.Sprintf("%s: Marshal: %v", job.Name, err))
					continue
				}
				stored := &actions_model.ActionRunJob{ID: 1, WorkflowPayload: payload}
				back, err := stored.ParseJob()
				if err != nil {
					problems = append(problems, fmt.Sprintf("%s: READ-BACK FAILS: %v", job.Name, err))
					continue
				}
				if len(back.Steps) != len(origRuns) {
					problems = append(problems, fmt.Sprintf("%s: steps %d -> %d", job.Name, len(origRuns), len(back.Steps)))
					continue
				}
				for i, s := range back.Steps {
					if s.Run != origRuns[i] {
						problems = append(problems, fmt.Sprintf("%s: step %d script changed %q -> %q", job.Name, i, origRuns[i], s.Run))
					}
				}
			}
			names := []string{}
			for _, wf := range wfs {
				_, job := wf.Job()
				names = append(names, fmt.Sprintf("%q on %q", job.Name, job.RunsOn()))
			}
			if len(problems) == 0 {
				t.Logf("%-42s => ok, %d job(s): %s", c.name, len(wfs), strings.Join(names, "; "))
			} else {
				t.Logf("%-42s => %d job(s), PROBLEMS: %s", c.name, len(wfs), strings.Join(problems, " | "))
			}
		}()
	}
}

lastPrompt: Reusable workflows and matrix jobs will be in almost every repo. Take real looking workflow files (multi-line run scripts, nested uses, matrix with if) through expansion, storing and reading back the…

content.text:
Yes to both: several GitHub-valid workflow shapes never start, and job count has no cap. I committed real workflow files into a test repo and drove them through detection, run insert, emitter passes, runner claim and completion; the probe is deleted and the tree is clean.

## Never starts

1. **A `run: |` script that begins with a blank line is stored in a form that cannot be read back.** The same happens when the first line is indented more than the rest (`|2`). The run is accepted and inserted, but the re-encoded job (`services/actions/run.go:143`, no read-back check) fails to parse on every runner claim.
   - **It also blocks the queue.** The claim error aborts the whole poll (`models/actions/task.go:286`), so a later job queued behind it stayed waiting through three polls. Any runner whose labels match the bad job gets nothing behind it until that job is cancelled.
   - Adding `name:` to the step does not help; I checked.

2. **One job with `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` inside a called workflow blocks the whole called workflow.** Children of a caller are always inserted blocked (`reusable_workflow.go:335`), so every one of them goes through the server-side `if:` evaluator, including jobs without `needs:`. The emitter panicked and `ci`, `test` and `report` all stayed blocked; only the unrelated top-level job ran.

3. **A step-level `continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental }}` makes the whole file invalid.** The step field is a plain bool (`modules/actions/jobparser/model.go:164`), so the workflow is rejected at detection and never triggers, with only a log warning.

4. **A caller secret that is anything other than exactly `${{ secrets.NAME }}` fails expansion.** With `token: ${{ secrets.A || secrets.B }}` and no `needs:`, no run was created at all. Behind `needs: build`, the emitter failed on every pass, which also left an unrelated `docs` job in the same run blocked.

5. **A boolean input whose default is an expression means no run is created.** Defaults are never evaluated (`workflow_call.go:222`). A string default such as `${{ github.sha }}` is passed to the called workflow as that literal text.

6. **Jobs in a called workflow gated on the triggering event are skipped.** `github.event_name` is forced to `workflow_call` for children (`services/actions/context.go:125`, marked FIXME), so `if: github.event_name == 'push' && …` was skipped on a push.

## Runs when it should not

7. **`if:` on a caller job with no `needs:` is ignored.** `deploy-prod` with `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/release'` on a master push was expanded and its deploy job ran (`run.go:218`). With `needs:` the condition is evaluated.

## Grows without limit

8. **There is no cap on jobs per run.** Four small files with a 5-way matrix at each of four levels produced 780 job rows in three emitter passes. `MaxJobNumPerRun = 256` exists but is never checked (`models/actions/run_job.go:27`). Nesting is capped at nine levels, so fan-out is unbounded at each of them.

9. **A failing expansion is retried indefinitely.** In item 4, every emitter pass hit the same error. From reading the queue code, the item is pushed back after about a second each time; I did not run the queue loop itself. The retries stop only once the caller is cancelled, by hand or by the 24h cron.

10. **Re-run gives matrix children with the same display name the same internal ID.** With `name: Test ${{ matrix.os }}` over an os × node matrix, the first attempt had IDs 2–5; after a re-run two rows shared 4 and two shared 5. From reading the re-run code, selecting one of those jobs later will select both.

## Held up

- **Scripts:** heredocs, tabs, trailing spaces, CRLF files, folded scalars and unicode all round-tripped unchanged.
- **YAML features:** anchors, merge keys, services and containers were fine.
- **Matrices:** include/exclude and matrices of objects and lists expanded correctly.
- **Callers:** a matrix on the caller with `with: ${{ matrix.env }}`, a typed boolean input used in a child `if:`, and a downstream `needs:` on the caller all worked.

Fix item 1 first: one such file stalls every other job behind it for the runners that match.

input.description: Probe commit-status collisions for same-named jobs, then clean up

content.text:
The context for both run types is mostly right, but three things around it are wrong: a `pull_request_target` run can execute a fork's copy of a called workflow with your secrets, a re-run job cannot see the earlier attempt's artifacts, and same-named jobs overwrite each other's commit status. I built the real task payloads (context, secrets, needs) for each case in a throwaway test; it is deleted and the tree is clean.

## pull_request_target

1. **A local `uses: ./…` in a `pull_request_target` workflow is read from the PR head, not the base.** The run records the PR head commit as the workflow's source commit (`services/actions/notifier_helper.go:342`), and local reusable workflows are resolved from that commit (`reusable_workflow.go:48`). With a fork PR that changed the called file, the child job created was the fork's version. The run needed no approval, and that job was handed `DEPLOY_KEY` through `secrets: inherit`.

2. **The token is read-only while secrets are released.** For the fork PR the job token had no issues or pull-request access and read-only code (`models/actions/token_permissions.go:54`). So label and comment workflows, the usual reason to use this trigger, will fail on fork PRs. This may be deliberate hardening, but it is inconsistent with handing over all secrets.

3. **The context values themselves were correct.** `event_name`, `ref` (base branch), `sha` (base head), `base_ref` and `actor` all came out right for the top-level job.

## Schedule

4. **`github.event` is the push that registered the schedule, with `schedule` added.** The job saw that push's `pusher`, `head_commit` and `commits`. When the schedule is registered through the bot or re-detection path instead, `github.event` contains only `schedule` and `github.event.repository` is missing. The stored run event also differs between the two paths ("push" vs "schedule").

5. **`github.sha` is the commit at registration, not the branch head.** When I moved the default branch without re-registering, the job got the old commit. Normal pushes re-register, so this bites in the `[skip ci]` case from my first report.

6. **Changing or renaming the default branch deletes the schedules and nothing re-creates them** (`services/repository/branch.go:462`, `:717`). This is from reading; I could not run that path from the test package. Schedules would stop until the next push to the new default branch.

`github.actor` is `gitea-actions` for scheduled runs, and they post no commit statuses; both look intentional.

## Re-run attempt

7. **A re-run job sees none of the earlier attempt's artifacts.** Every artifact query for a job token filters on the job's own attempt (`routers/api/actions/artifactsv4.go:588`, `:642`; `artifacts.go:346`). After "re-run failed jobs" on a build → deploy run, deploy in attempt 2 saw an empty list, although the `dist` artifact from build was still stored. I ran the handler's query, not the HTTP endpoint. Any deploy job that downloads a build artifact will fail on a partial re-run.

8. **Everything else carried over correctly.** `needs.build.outputs` and the result came through from the first attempt. `run_attempt` was 2, `triggering_actor` was the re-running user and `actor` the original. Commit statuses were re-pointed at the new attempt's jobs, with deploy back to pending.

## Commit statuses

9. **Jobs with the same name share one status, so a failure can show as success.** A matrix caller deploying to dev, prod and staging produced a single `deploy / deploy (push)` status. Prod failed, and the status ended as success because staging's job was written last. The caller rows themselves were correct (`release / rollout (prod) (push)` = failure). If the shared name is a required check, the failure is hidden.
   - Statuses for jobs inside a called workflow are named after the called workflow, not the workflow that ran.

10. **Those colliding statuses are rewritten on every emitter pass.** The run wrote 31 status rows; three further passes with nothing to do added nine more.

Fix item 1 first: it gives a fork PR your secrets without approval.

cat > routers/api/actions/runner/zz_probe_test.go <<'EOF'
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package runner

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"

	runnerv1 "gitea.dev/actions-proto-go/runner/v1"
	actions_model "gitea.dev/models/actions"
	"gitea.dev/models/db"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	"gitea.dev/modules/queue"
	"gitea.dev/modules/setting"
	actions_service "gitea.dev/services/actions"

	"connectrpc.com/connect"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
	"google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/timestamppb"
)

func TestMain(m *testing.M) { unittest.MainTest(m) }

var (
	pOnce  sync.Once
	pIndex int
)

const pWorkflow = `name: ci
on: push
concurrency:
  group: prod
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: probe-linux
    steps:
      - name: Compile
        run: make
      - name: Package
        run: make dist
  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: probe-linux
    steps:
      - run: ./deploy.sh
`

type probe struct {
	t      *testing.T
	ctx    context.Context
	rctx   context.Context
	runner *actions_model.ActionRunner
	svc    *Service
}

func newProbe(t *testing.T, cancellingSupport bool) *probe {
	require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
	setting.Actions.Enabled = true
	setting.Actions.MaxConcurrentTaskPicks = 16
	setting.Actions.ZombieTaskTimeout = 10 * time.Minute
	setting.Actions.EndlessTaskTimeout = 3 * time.Hour
	setting.Actions.AbandonedJobTimeout = 24 * time.Hour
	pOnce.Do(func() { require.NoError(t, actions_service.Init(t.Context())) })
	pIndex++
	r := &actions_model.ActionRunner{UUID: fmt.Sprintf("11111111-2222-3333-4444-%012d", pIndex), Name: "probe", RepoID: 4, AgentLabels: []string{"probe-linux"}, HasCancellingSupport: cancellingSupport}
	r.GenerateAndFillToken()
	require.NoError(t, db.Insert(t.Context(), r))
	return &probe{t: t, ctx: t.Context(), rctx: context.WithValue(t.Context(), runnerCtxKey{}, r), runner: r, svc: &Service{}}
}

func (p *probe) flush() { _ = queue.GetManager().FlushAll(p.ctx, 5*time.Second) }

func (p *probe) push() *actions_model.ActionRun {
	run := &actions_model.ActionRun{
		Title: "probe", RepoID: 4, OwnerID: 5, WorkflowID: "ci.yml", TriggerUserID: 5, Ref: "refs/heads/master",
		CommitSHA: "c2d72f548424103f01ee1dc02889c1e2bff816b0", Event: "push", TriggerEvent: "push", EventPayload: "{}",
		WorkflowRepoID: 4, WorkflowCommitSHA: "c2d72f548424103f01ee1dc02889c1e2bff816b0",
	}
	require.NoError(p.t, actions_service.PrepareRunAndInsert(p.ctx, []byte(pWorkflow), run, nil))
	p.flush()
	return run
}

func (p *probe) fetch() *runnerv1.Task {
	resp, err := p.svc.FetchTask(p.rctx, connect.NewRequest(&runnerv1.FetchTaskRequest{}))
	require.NoError(p.t, err)
	p.flush()
	return resp.Msg.Task
}

func (p *probe) logs(taskID int64, lines ...string) error {
	task, err := actions_model.GetTaskByID(p.ctx, taskID)
	require.NoError(p.t, err)
	rows := make([]*runnerv1.LogRow, 0, len(lines))
	for _, l := range lines {
		rows = append(rows, &runnerv1.LogRow{Time: timestamppb.Now(), Content: l})
	}
	_, err = p.svc.UpdateLog(p.rctx, connect.NewRequest(&runnerv1.UpdateLogRequest{TaskId: taskID, Index: task.LogLength, Rows: rows}))
	return err
}

// report sends a state report; result UNSPECIFIED is a heartbeat. It returns what the server answers.
func (p *probe) report(taskID int64, result runnerv1.Result) string {
	st := &runnerv1.TaskState{Id: taskID, Result: result, Steps: []*runnerv1.StepState{{Id: 0, StartedAt: timestamppb.Now()}}}
	if result != runnerv1.Result_RESULT_UNSPECIFIED {
		st.StoppedAt = timestamppb.Now()
		st.Steps = []*runnerv1.StepState{{Id: 0, Result: result, StartedAt: timestamppb.Now(), StoppedAt: timestamppb.Now()}, {Id: 1, Result: result, StartedAt: timestamppb.Now(), StoppedAt: timestamppb.Now()}}
	}
	resp, err := p.svc.UpdateTask(p.rctx, connect.NewRequest(&runnerv1.UpdateTaskRequest{State: st}))
	p.flush()
	if err != nil {
		return "ERROR " + err.Error()
	}
	return strings.TrimPrefix(resp.Msg.State.Result.String(), "RESULT_")
}

// elapse moves the task's clocks back, i.e. lets wall-clock time pass with nothing touching the task.
func (p *probe) elapse(taskID int64, d time.Duration) {
	_, err := db.Exec(p.ctx, "UPDATE `action_task` SET updated = updated - ?, started = started - ? WHERE id = ?", int64(d.Seconds()), int64(d.Seconds()), taskID)
	require.NoError(p.t, err)
}

func (p *probe) cancel(run *actions_model.ActionRun) {
	var updated []*actions_model.ActionRunJob
	require.NoError(p.t, db.WithTx(p.ctx, func(ctx context.Context) error { // as the web Cancel handler does
		r, err := actions_model.GetRunByRepoAndID(ctx, 4, run.ID)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		jobs, err := actions_model.GetRunJobsByRunAndAttemptID(ctx, run.ID, r.LatestAttemptID)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		updated, err = actions_model.CancelJobs(ctx, jobs)
		return err
	}))
	actions_service.EmitJobsIfReadyByJobs(updated)
	p.flush()
}

func (p *probe) crons() {
	require.NoError(p.t, actions_service.StopZombieTasks(p.ctx))
	require.NoError(p.t, actions_service.StopEndlessTasks(p.ctx))
	require.NoError(p.t, actions_service.CancelAbandonedJobs(p.ctx))
	p.flush()
}

func (p *probe) state(run *actions_model.ActionRun) string {
	r, err := actions_model.GetRunByRepoAndID(p.ctx, 4, run.ID)
	require.NoError(p.t, err)
	jobs, err := actions_model.GetRunJobsByRunAndAttemptID(p.ctx, run.ID, r.LatestAttemptID)
	require.NoError(p.t, err)
	out := "run=" + r.Status.String()
	for _, j := range jobs {
		out += fmt.Sprintf(" %s=%s", j.JobID, j.Status)
		if j.TaskID > 0 {
			task, _ := actions_model.GetTaskByID(p.ctx, j.TaskID)
			steps, _ := actions_model.GetTaskStepsByTaskID(p.ctx, j.TaskID)
			ss := []string{}
			for _, s := range steps {
				ss = append(ss, s.Status.String())
			}
			out += fmt.Sprintf("[task=%s steps=%s logs_archived=%v]", task.Status, strings.Join(ss, "/"), task.LogInStorage)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func (p *probe) say(format string, args ...any) { p.t.Logf(format, args...) }

func TestProbe1RunnerDies(t *testing.T) {
	p := newProbe(t, false)
	run := p.push()
	task := p.fetch()
	require.NoError(t, p.logs(task.Id, "compiling...", "still compiling..."))
	p.report(task.Id, runnerv1.Result_RESULT_UNSPECIFIED)
	p.say("t+0   runner dies mid-step:        %s", p.state(run))
	p.elapse(task.Id, 9*time.Minute)

	}
	_, err = p.svc.UpdateLog(p.rctx, connect.NewRequest(&runnerv1.UpdateLogRequest{TaskId: taskID, Index: task.LogLength, Rows: rows}))
	return err
}

// report sends a state report; result UNSPECIFIED is a heartbeat. It returns what the server answers.
func (p *probe) report(taskID int64, result runnerv1.Result) string {
	st := &runnerv1.TaskState{Id: taskID, Result: result, Steps: []*runnerv1.StepState{{Id: 0, StartedAt: timestamppb.Now()}}}
	if result != runnerv1.Result_RESULT_UNSPECIFIED {
		st.StoppedAt = timestamppb.Now()
		st.Steps = []*runnerv1.StepState{{Id: 0, Result: result, StartedAt: timestamppb.Now(), StoppedAt: timestamppb.Now()}, {Id: 1, Result: result, StartedAt: timestamppb.Now(), StoppedAt: timestamppb.Now()}}
	}
	resp, err := p.svc.UpdateTask(p.rctx, connect.NewRequest(&runnerv1.UpdateTaskRequest{State: st}))
	p.flush()
	if err != nil {
		return "ERROR " + err.Error()
	}
	return strings.TrimPrefix(resp.Msg.State.Result.String(), "RESULT_")

	_, err := db.Exec(p.ctx, "UPDATE `action_task` SET updated = updated - ?, started = started - ? WHERE id = ?", int64(d.Seconds()), int64(d.Seconds()), taskID)

		r, err := actions_model.GetRunByRepoAndID(ctx, 4, run.ID)

	p.flush()

	}
	return out

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package runner

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"

	runnerv1 "gitea.dev/actions-proto-go/runner/v1"
	actions_model "gitea.dev/models/actions"
	"gitea.dev/models/db"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	"gitea.dev/modules/queue"
	"gitea.dev/modules/setting"
	actions_service "gitea.dev/services/actions"

	"connectrpc.com/connect"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
	"google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/timestamppb"
)

func TestMain(m *testing.M) { unittest.MainTest(m) }

var (
	pOnce  sync.Once
	pIndex int
)

const pWorkflow = `name: ci
on: push
concurrency:
  group: prod
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: probe-linux
    steps:
      - name: Compile
        run: make
      - name: Package
        run: make dist
  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: probe-linux
    steps:
      - run: ./deploy.sh
`

type probe struct {
	t      *testing.T
	ctx    context.Context
	rctx   context.Context
	runner *actions_model.ActionRunner
	svc    *Service
}

func newProbe(t *testing.T, cancellingSupport bool) *probe {
	require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
	setting.Actions.Enabled = true
	setting.Actions.MaxConcurrentTaskPicks = 16
	setting.Actions.ZombieTaskTimeout = 10 * time.Minute
	setting.Actions.EndlessTaskTimeout = 3 * time.Hour
	setting.Actions.AbandonedJobTimeout = 24 * time.Hour
	pOnce.Do(func() { require.NoError(t, actions_service.Init(t.Context())) })
	pIndex++
	r := &actions_model.ActionRunner{UUID: fmt.Sprintf("11111111-2222-3333-4444-%012d", pIndex), Name: "probe", RepoID: 4, AgentLabels: []string{"probe-linux"}, HasCancellingSupport: cancellingSupport}
	r.GenerateAndFillToken()
	require.NoError(t, db.Insert(t.Context(), r))
	return &probe{t: t, ctx: t.Context(), rctx: context.WithValue(t.Context(), runnerCtxKey{}, r), runner: r, svc: &Service{}}
}

func (p *probe) flush() { _ = queue.GetManager().FlushAll(p.ctx, 5*time.Second) }

func (p *probe) push() *actions_model.ActionRun {
	run := &actions_model.ActionRun{
		Title: "probe", RepoID: 4, OwnerID: 5, WorkflowID: "ci.yml", TriggerUserID: 5, Ref: "refs/heads/master",
		CommitSHA: "c2d72f548424103f01ee1dc02889c1e2bff816b0", Event: "push", TriggerEvent: "push", EventPayload: "{}",
		WorkflowRepoID: 4, WorkflowCommitSHA: "c2d72f548424103f01ee1dc02889c1e2bff816b0",
	}
	require.NoError(p.t, actions_service.PrepareRunAndInsert(p.ctx, []byte(pWorkflow), run, nil))
	p.flush()
	return run
}

func (p *probe) fetch() *runnerv1.Task {
	resp, err := p.svc.FetchTask(p.rctx, connect.NewRequest(&runnerv1.FetchTaskRequest{}))
	require.NoError(p.t, err)
	p.flush()
	return resp.Msg.Task
}

func (p *probe) logs(taskID int64, lines ...string) error {
	task, err := actions_model.GetTaskByID(p.ctx, taskID)
	require.NoError(p.t, err)
	rows := make([]*runnerv1.LogRow, 0, len(lines))
	for _, l := range lines {
		rows = append(rows, &runnerv1.LogRow{Time: timestamppb.Now(), Content: l})
	}
	_, err = p.svc.UpdateLog(p.rctx, connect.NewRequest(&runnerv1.UpdateLogRequest{TaskId: taskID, Index: task.LogLength, Rows: rows}))
	return err
}

// report sends a state report; result UNSPECIFIED is a heartbeat. It returns what the server answers.
func (p *probe) report(taskID int64, result runnerv1.Result) string {
	st := &runnerv1.TaskState{Id: taskID, Result: result, Steps: []*runnerv1.StepState{{Id: 0, StartedAt: timestamppb.Now()}}}
	if result != runnerv1.Result_RESULT_UNSPECIFIED {
		st.StoppedAt = timestamppb.Now()
		st.Steps = []*runnerv1.StepState{{Id: 0, Result: result, StartedAt: timestamppb.Now(), StoppedAt: timestamppb.Now()}, {Id: 1, Result: result, StartedAt: timestamppb.Now(), StoppedAt: timestamppb.Now()}}
	}
	resp, err := p.svc.UpdateTask(p.rctx, connect.NewRequest(&runnerv1.UpdateTaskRequest{State: st}))
	p.flush()
	if err != nil {
		return "ERROR " + err.Error()
	}
	return strings.TrimPrefix(resp.Msg.State.Result.String(), "RESULT_")
}

// elapse moves the task's clocks back, i.e. lets wall-clock time pass with nothing touching the task.
func (p *probe) elapse(taskID int64, d time.Duration) {
	_, err := db.Exec(p.ctx, "UPDATE `action_task` SET updated = updated - ?, started = started - ? WHERE id = ?", int64(d.Seconds()), int64(d.Seconds()), taskID)
	require.NoError(p.t, err)
}

func (p *probe) cancel(run *actions_model.ActionRun) {
	var updated []*actions_model.ActionRunJob
	require.NoError(p.t, db.WithTx(p.ctx, func(ctx context.Context) error { // as the web Cancel handler does
		r, err := actions_model.GetRunByRepoAndID(ctx, 4, run.ID)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		jobs, err := actions_model.GetRunJobsByRunAndAttemptID(ctx, run.ID, r.LatestAttemptID)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		updated, err = actions_model.CancelJobs(ctx, jobs)
		return err
	}))
	actions_service.EmitJobsIfReadyByJobs(updated)
	p.flush()
}

func (p *probe) crons() {
	require.NoError(p.t, actions_service.StopZombieTasks(p.ctx))
	require.NoError(p.t, actions_service.StopEndlessTasks(p.ctx))
	require.NoError(p.t, actions_service.CancelAbandonedJobs(p.ctx))
	p.flush()
}

func (p *probe) state(run *actions_model.ActionRun) string {
	r, err := actions_model.GetRunByRepoAndID(p.ctx, 4, run.ID)
	require.NoError(p.t, err)
	jobs, err := actions_model.GetRunJobsByRunAndAttemptID(p.ctx, run.ID, r.LatestAttemptID)
	require.NoError(p.t, err)
	out := "run=" + r.Status.String()
	for _, j := range jobs {
		out += fmt.Sprintf(" %s=%s", j.JobID, j.Status)
		if j.TaskID > 0 {
			task, _ := actions_model.GetTaskByID(p.ctx, j.TaskID)
			steps, _ := actions_model.GetTaskStepsByTaskID(p.ctx, j.TaskID)
			ss := []string{}
			for _, s := range steps {
				ss = append(ss, s.Status.String())
			}
			out += fmt.Sprintf("[task=%s steps=%s logs_archived=%v]", task.Status, strings.Join(ss, "/"), task.LogInStorage)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func (p *probe) say(format string, args ...any) { p.t.Logf(format, args...) }

func TestProbe1RunnerDies(t *testing.T) {
	p := newProbe(t, false)
	run := p.push()
	task := p.fetch()
	require.NoError(t, p.logs(task.Id, "compiling...", "still compiling..."))
	p.report(task.Id, runnerv1.Result_RESULT_UNSPECIFIED)
	p.say("t+0   runner dies mid-step:        %s", p.state(run))
	p.elapse(task.Id, 9*time.Minute)
	p.crons()
	p.say("t+9m  crons:                       %s", p.state(run))
	p.elapse(task.Id, 2*time.Minute)
	p.crons()
	p.say("t+11m crons:                       %s", p.state(run))
}

func TestProbe2RunnerDiesThenCancel(t *testing.T) {
	for _, support := range []bool{false, true} {
		p := newProbe(t, support)
		run := p.push()
		task := p.fetch()
		p.report(task.Id, runnerv1.Result_RESULT_UNSPECIFIED)
		p.elapse(task.Id, 3*time.Minute) // runner has been dead for 3 minutes
		p.cancel(run)
		p.say("runner cancelling-capable=%v: cancel 3m after it died:  %s", support, p.state(run))
		if !support {
			continue
		}
		next := p.push()
		p.say("    next push in the same concurrency group:          %s", p.state(next))
		p.elapse(task.Id, 9*time.Minute)
		p.crons()
		p.say("    9m after the cancel, crons:                       %s", p.state(run))
		p.cancel(run) // someone clicks cancel again
		p.elapse(task.Id, 9*time.Minute)
		p.crons()
		p.say("    cancel clicked again, 9m later (18m total), crons: %s", p.state(run))
		p.elapse(task.Id, 2*time.Minute)
		p.crons()
		p.say("    2m more with no clicks, crons:                    %s | next push: %s", p.state(run), p.state(next))
	}
}

func TestProbe3GiteaDownElevenMinutes(t *testing.T) {
	p := newProbe(t, true)
	run := p.push()
	task := p.fetch()
	p.report(task.Id, runnerv1.Result_RESULT_UNSPECIFIED)
	p.elapse(task.Id, 11*time.Minute) // Gitea is down; the runner is alive and keeps working
	p.crons()                         // all three crons are RunAtStart
	p.say("Gitea back after 11m, start-up crons:     %s", p.state(run))
	p.say("runner's next heartbeat is answered with:  %s   (the runner only aborts on CANCELLED)", p.report(task.Id, runnerv1.Result_RESULT_UNSPECIFIED))
	p.say("runner sends more log lines:               err=%v", p.logs(task.Id, "deploying..."))
	p.say("runner finishes and reports SUCCESS, answered: %s", p.report(task.Id, runnerv1.Result_RESULT_SUCCESS))
	p.say("final:                                     %s", p.state(run))
}

func TestProbe4JobFinishesWhileGiteaDown(t *testing.T) {
	p := newProbe(t, true)
	run := p.push()
	task := p.fetch()
	p.report(task.Id, runnerv1.Result_RESULT_UNSPECIFIED)
	// Gitea goes down for 2 minutes; the job finishes during it and the runner's final report is never delivered
	p.elapse(task.Id, 2*time.Minute)
	p.crons()
	p.say("Gitea back after 2m, start-up crons: %s", p.state(run))
	other := p.push()
	p.say("the same runner polls again:         got a new task=%v; old run still: %s | new run: %s", p.fetch() != nil, p.state(run), p.state(other))
	p.elapse(task.Id, 9*time.Minute)
	p.crons()
	p.say("11m after the last heartbeat, crons: %s", p.state(run))
}

func TestProbe5CrashMidReport(t *testing.T) {
	p := newProbe(t, false)
	run := p.push()
	task := p.fetch()
	p.report(task.Id, runnerv1.Result_RESULT_UNSPECIFIED)
	// The process is killed inside UpdateTaskByState after the task row was written and before the job row was:
	_, err := db.Exec(p.ctx, "UPDATE `action_task` SET status = ?, stopped = ? WHERE id = ?", actions_model.StatusSuccess, time.Now().Unix(), task.Id)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	p.say("crash between task write and job write:    %s", p.state(run))
	p.say("after restart the runner retries its final report, answered: %s", p.report(task.Id, runnerv1.Result_RESULT_SUCCESS))
	p.say("after the retry:                           %s", p.state(run))
	p.elapse(task.Id, 30*time.Hour)
	_, err = db.Exec(p.ctx, "UPDATE `action_run_job` SET updated = updated - ? WHERE run_id = ?", 30*3600, run.ID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	p.crons()
	p.say("30h later, all three crons:                %s", p.state(run))
	p.cancel(run)
	p.say("user cancels:                              %s", p.state(run))
	next := p.push()
	p.say("next push in the same concurrency group:   %s", p.state(next))
}

func TestProbe6CancelThenRestart(t *testing.T) {
	for _, support := range []bool{false, true} {
		p := newProbe(t, support)
		run := p.push()
		task := p.fetch()
		p.report(task.Id, runnerv1.Result_RESULT_UNSPECIFIED)
		p.cancel(run)
		p.elapse(task.Id, 2*time.Minute) // Gitea restarts right after the cancel, 2 minutes down
		p.crons()
		p.say("cancelling-capable=%v: cancel, then 2m restart: %s", support, p.state(run))
		p.say("    runner's heartbeat after restart answered: %s", p.report(task.Id, runnerv1.Result_RESULT_UNSPECIFIED))
		p.say("    runner cleans up and reports FAILURE, answered: %s", p.report(task.Id, runnerv1.Result_RESULT_FAILURE))
		p.say("    final: %s", p.state(run))
	}
}

func TestProbe7ClaimedButNeverDelivered(t *testing.T) {
	p := newProbe(t, false)
	run := p.push()
	task := p.fetch() // Gitea is killed before this response reaches the runner
	p.elapse(task.Id, 11*time.Minute)
	p.crons()
	p.say("job claimed, response lost in a restart; 11m later: %s", p.state(run))
}

content.text:
The state ends up wrong in four of the seven points I walked through, and two of those never heal. I drove the real `FetchTask`, `UpdateLog` and `UpdateTask` handlers, cancel, and all three crons through each point in a throwaway test (deleted; tree is clean), moving the task's clocks back to simulate elapsed time.

The crons run at start-up as well as on a timer (`services/cron/tasks_actions.go:26`). The zombie cron fires after 10 minutes without a report and ticks every 5 minutes, so "10–15 min" below is that window.

| Point | What it shows meanwhile | How long | Ends as |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runner dies mid-step | job running | 10–15 min | failure, dependents skipped (as designed) |
| Runner dead, then cancel (plain runner) | — | immediate | cancelled (correct) |
| Runner dead, then cancel (cancelling-capable runner) | cancelling, group held | 10–15 min after the *last* cancel click | cancelled |
| Gitea down ≥10 min, runner alive | — | at start-up | failure, **permanent, wrong** |
| Job finishes while Gitea is down | running, group held | 10–15 min | failure, **permanent, wrong** |
| Crash between the task write and the job write | job running, task success | forever | **never resolves** |
| Job claimed, response lost in a restart | running | 10–15 min | failure, never ran |

Cancel followed by a 2-minute restart came out correct for both runner types.

## Where it goes wrong

1. **A Gitea outage of 10 minutes or more fails every in-flight job at start-up.**
   - The zombie cron runs during start-up, before runners can report (code reading; the probe called the cron directly). With an 11-minute gap it failed the job and skipped its dependent while the runner was still working.
   - The runner's next heartbeat was answered `FAILURE`, and its eventual `SUCCESS` was ignored. From reading the runner (v1.0.8, not executed), it only aborts on `CANCELLED`, so the job keeps executing and a re-run starts a second copy.

2. **A job that finishes while Gitea is down is recorded as failed.**
   - From reading the runner, the final report is retried for a bounded time (30s with the fallback value in that code) and then dropped.
   - Server-side the job stayed "running" after a 2-minute outage. A new push in the same concurrency group was blocked behind it, and 11 minutes after the last heartbeat the cron marked it failure and skipped deploy. A deploy that succeeded would show as failed, and re-running repeats it.

3. **A crash between the two writes of a final report leaves the job running forever.**
   - `UpdateTaskByState` writes the task, then the job, with no transaction (`models/actions/task.go:494`). I set that intermediate state by SQL, since I can't kill the process mid-function.
   - The runner's retry was answered `SUCCESS` and changed nothing, because a finished task returns early (`:480`).
   - Thirty hours of all three crons left the job running, and a user cancel did nothing.
   - The next push in the same concurrency group stayed blocked; the group is held permanently.
   - Any error between those two writes gives the same state.

4. **Each cancel click on a dead runner's job restarts the 10-minute clock.**
   - This applies to cancelling-capable runners. Cancel updates the task row (`task.go:580`), which is what the zombie cron measures. Nine minutes after a cancel it was still cancelling; a second click bought another nine; it only cleared 11 minutes after the last click.
   - Until then the run is not done, so it can't be re-run, and the next push in its concurrency group stayed blocked.

5. **A job claimed just before a restart fails without ever running.** The task exists but the response never reached a runner; 11 minutes later it was failure with its dependent skipped.

## Correction to my cancel/re-run answer

I said a "cancelling" job could only be cleared by the 3-hour endless-task timeout. That came from simulating a runner that keeps heart-beating. Reading the runner code, it stops heart-beating once cancelled, so the zombie cron clears it 10–15 minutes after the last cancel click.

The runner version vendored here (v1.0.8) does not advertise the cancelling capability, so with it cancel is immediate. The `has_cancelling_support` column on the runner table shows what your fleet reports.

func TestProbeDefaultBranchSchedules(t *testing.T) {
	require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
	ctx := t.Context()
	dir := repo_model.RepoPath("user5", "repo4")
	git := func(env []string, stdin string, args ...string) string {
		cmd := exec.Command("git", args...)
		cmd.Dir = dir
		cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), env...)
		cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(stdin)
		var out, errb bytes.Buffer
		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &out, &errb
		require.NoError(t, cmd.Run(), "git %v: %s", args, errb.String())
		return strings.TrimSpace(out.String())
	}
	env := []string{"GIT_INDEX_FILE=" + filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "index"), "GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=p", "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=p@example.com", "GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=p", "GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=p@example.com"}
	blob := git(env, "name: nightly\non:\n  schedule:\n    - cron: '0 3 * * *'\njobs:\n  build:\n    runs-on: probe-linux\n    steps:\n      - run: make nightly\n", "hash-object", "-w", "--stdin")
	git(env, "", "update-index", "--add", "--cacheinfo", "100644,"+blob+",.gitea/workflows/nightly.yml")
	sha := git(env, "", "commit-tree", git(env, "", "write-tree"), "-m", "nightly")
	git(nil, "", "update-ref", "refs/heads/master", sha)
	git(nil, "", "update-ref", "refs/heads/develop", sha) // the same commit, so the workflow exists on the new default branch too

	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 4})
	count := func() int64 {
		n, err := db.GetEngine(ctx).Where("repo_id = 4").Count(new(actions_model.ActionSchedule))
		require.NoError(t, err)
		return n
	}
	require.NoError(t, actions_service.DetectAndHandleSchedules(ctx, repo))
	t.Logf("default branch %q: schedules registered = %d", repo.DefaultBranch, count())
	require.NoError(t, SetRepoDefaultBranch(ctx, repo, "develop"))
	repo = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 4})
	t.Logf("default branch changed to %q (same commit, nightly.yml still present): schedules registered = %d", repo.DefaultBranch, count())
}

content.text:
Every finding has now been executed except one detail: that the start-up zombie sweep runs before runners can report (item 6) is still code reading only. The test files are deleted and the tree is clean. Running the runner module's tests downloaded its dependencies and a Go 1.26.0 toolchain into the Go module cache.

Everything ran on SQLite in the unit-test harness, with runner code exercised in isolation. Nothing ran against Postgres/MySQL, a live server or a real runner process.

## One list, worst first

**Secrets exposure or instance-wide stall**

1. **Fork PR review runs the fork's workflow with secrets** (ran). An untrusted author who would normally need approval left a comment review; the run needed no approval and was handed `DEPLOY_KEY`.
2. **`pull_request_target` with a local `uses:` runs the fork's copy of the called file with secrets** (ran).
3. **A `run: |` script starting with a blank line blocks the runner queue** (ran). The job can't be read back, and every matching runner's poll fails behind it.
4. **One broken scheduled workflow stops older schedules in other repos** (ran). Three cron ticks started nothing for the other repo.
5. **`cancelled()` in a job `if:` panics the emitter** (ran). The run sticks, other runs in the batch lose their update, and inside a called workflow every child is blocked.
6. **A Gitea outage of 10+ minutes fails every in-flight job at start-up** (ran; start-up ordering read only). The runner keeps executing: it only aborts on `CANCELLED` (ran).

**Wrong results, double deploys, security gaps**

7. **Approval gate bypass through the emitter** (ran).
8. **Task token still valid after the task ends** (ran).
9. **"Re-run failed jobs" with nothing failed re-runs everything** (ran).
10. **`if:` on a caller job without `needs:` is ignored**, so the called workflow runs (ran).
11. **Same-named jobs share one commit status**, so a failure can show as success (ran).
12. **A job that finishes while Gitea is down is recorded as failed** (ran). The runner gave up after 60 seconds.
13. **Zombie and endless crons mark the job failed but don't stop the runner** (ran).
14. **A crash between the task write and the job write leaves the job running forever**, holding its concurrency group (ran, state injected).
15. **A re-run job can't see the earlier attempt's artifacts** (ran, handler's query).
16. **Two jobs in one concurrency group that become ready together deadlock for 24h** (ran).
17. **Approving a run that isn't pending corrupts it** (ran).
18. **Re-running a run cancelled while awaiting approval starts it unapproved** (ran).

**Valid workflows that never start, skip or stick**

19. **Step-level `continue-on-error: ${{ }}` makes the whole file ignored** (ran).
20. **`runs-on` from a list or from `needs` gets an unmatchable label; dynamic matrices aren't expanded** (ran).
21. **A caller secret not written exactly as `${{ secrets.NAME }}` fails expansion** (ran). There is no run, or the run sticks, blocks sibling jobs and is retried about every 1.5s.
22. **Server-side `if:` gets wrong data** (ran): `needs.*.result` never matches, several `github.*` fields are empty, and boolean dispatch inputs are strings.
23. **`github.event_name` is `workflow_call` inside called workflows**, so event-gated jobs skip (ran).
24. **A boolean input default written as an expression means no run** (ran).
25. **`if:` evaluation errors leave the job blocked instead of failed** (ran).
26. **`pull_request_target` token is read-only while secrets are released** (ran).
27. **No cap on jobs per run** (ran, 780 rows from four files).
28. **Matrix outputs are lost if a later leg reports none** (ran).
29. **"Re-run failed jobs" re-runs a whole called workflow** (ran).
30. **Cancel misses a job being claimed at that moment** (ran as a real race). Two related variants, overwriting a finished caller and children of a cancelled caller starting, ran with injected state.
31. **Each cancel click on a dead runner's job resets the 10-minute clock** (ran).
32. **The abandoned-job cron cancels blocked jobs whose dependency is still running** (ran).
33. **A job claimed just before a restart fails without running** (ran).
34. **Schedules go stale or vanish** (ran):
    - a `[skip ci]` push leaves a deleted workflow scheduled;
    - changing the default branch deletes all schedules;
    - disabling Actions leaves scheduled runs queued;
    - 120 due schedules started 70, then 50.
35. **Scheduled runs get the registering push as `github.event`, and its commit as `github.sha`** (ran).
36. **Job-level `concurrency:` inside a called workflow is ignored** (ran).
37. **PR label removal fires `labeled`; `unlabeled` never fires** (ran).
38. **Duplicate child IDs after a re-run** (ran). Re-running one failed leg also re-ran a leg that had passed.
39. **A failed run-status update is never retried**, so the run can stay "running" (ran, forced failure).

**Noise**

40. **Job name with an expression becomes the literal status name** (ran).
41. **Cancel sends duplicate job notifications** (ran, two each for child jobs).
42. **Colliding statuses are rewritten on every emitter pass** (ran).

## Things I called fine, re-checked

- **Stored jobs round-trip unchanged.** I had only compared script text. I now compared every field the runner reads (172 fields across five files, including look-alike values such as `"3.10"`, `"yes"`, `"0123"`, containers, services, anchors and CRLF). All identical.
- **Matrix values survive storage.** Thirteen legs with mixed types (`18`, `"20"`, `"1e3"`, `true`, `"true"`, null) kept their types.
- **Double re-run produces one attempt.** I had tested it sequentially. Fifteen rounds of six simultaneous re-runs each gave exactly one new attempt and no stray rows.
- **`pull_request_target` context.** I had used a hand-built payload. With the real converter on a fixture PR, `ref`, `sha`, `base_ref` and `head_ref` were all correct.
- **Nesting cap and cycle detection.** I had quoted the cap from the constant. An 11-level chain stopped with an error past level 9, and an A→B→A cycle was detected. Both surface as expansion errors, so they stick and retry like item 21.

One re-check got worse: I had described the cancel-versus-claim race (item 30) as narrow. Racing a real cancel against a real runner poll, the cancel reported nothing cancelled and the job kept running in 133 of 150 rounds. SQLite serialises writers, which inflates that rate, but the logic is the same on any database.

Two corrections to earlier answers: the runner drops its final report after about 60 seconds, not 30, and the fork-review finding (item 1) is no longer reading only.
